why: D-SINK-85 (owner, 2026-11-06). Byte copies of the code each Omarchy host runs over a notification body,
so the plugin's own bodies can be run through it in node (tests/Model.test.js) and in Qt's engine
(tests/Model.spec.qml). A copy is only evidence while it IS the host's file: every copy below is pinned
by sha256, the node loader (tests/Model.test.js) refuses a copy whose bytes are not its pin, and
tests/test_notify_hosts.py holds each pin to its source -- the member of the cached omarchy package it
was taken from, and for the host that is installed, the file under OMARCHY_SHELL_DIR
(/usr/share/omarchy/shell). The QML spec imports the copies as they are on disk (a TestCase cannot read
a file's bytes) and trusts those two checks, both of which the gate runs.
A red there after an Omarchy update is a re-measurement request: re-copy
the changed file, re-pin it, and see whether tests/fixtures/notify-hosts/cases.js still draws as
4.0.6's NotificationLogic.js carries em dashes in its comments, so its copy sits under a directory
named nonascii, the ASCII gate's one exemption by tree; the 4.5.0 files are ASCII.
